title: Sand
description: An album cover pressed out of coloured sand. Drag across it to crumble grains into a dune, then press and hold: the picture softens into beads, the sand lifts in loose amorphous clumps on small soft arcs, drifts like sand settling in water and comes to rest from the bottom up, every grain on the pixel of the next record that best matches its colour. Collapse into next lets the record slide into strata first, and Shift with hold or R rebuilds the current cover.
intent: One material finished to the edge: a real cover you wear away grain by grain, then watch its settled sand erupt and land as the next record.

changelog.summary:
Hold, double-click, R and the Rebuild as next button now morph the tray into the next cover instead of pulling grains back home
New sandMorph.js matches every grain to a next-cover pixel colour first (three luminance-plus-chroma bin passes, then a pooled luminance rank pass) and proximity second (Hilbert-curve order inside each bin), as a strict one-to-one plan in about 5ms for 57,600 grains
Grains fly in amorphous clumps: warped tiles share a centroid path, gather mid-flight and bloom into place, ride a shared two-octave curl-noise drift, and leave in a smooth noise-plus-distance stagger from the press point
The intact picture loosens into beaded sand over 180ms before lifting off, and gather and launch are split over two frames to stay inside the frame budget
Each grain gets its own flight time scaled by distance, so short hops settle sooner and long arcs take longer
The next cover is preloaded and staged into the spare texture slot while idle, so the morph starts immediately; if it has not loaded, the hold falls back to the old return home
Next cover keeps its strata collapse but erupts with the same colour-matched, clumped morph
Copy updated: hint, Rebuild as next button (buttons wrap in narrow columns), tray aria-label and page description
Clumps now hold together in flight: each warped tile shares one departure time (the average of its grains) and one flight duration taken from its centroid span, written into a 13-float record and read by a new aClumpTime attribute
The shader drives the clump centre with the shared clump time and uses each grain's own time only for the bloom and colour blend; grains keep their starting spacing until 55% of the flight, cohesion rose from 0.38 to 0.6, and the curl drift carries on through the bloom so blobs open up as they land
Each grain's own flight is stretched so it never lands before its clump, and grains caught mid-air form their own clumps so they never hang waiting for the dune
Warped tile ids, clump noise and per-pixel jitter are precomputed per cell when the grid is built, so the launch frame no longer runs noise or hashes per grain
Gather and match, flight planning, and buffer upload now run on three separate frames for both the hold morph and the strata eruption
Staging the next cover waits for an idle callback (with a timeout fallback), skips while the pointer is down, and splits the texture upload and the cell sampling across two idle callbacks
If the next cover is not ready when a hold completes, the picture still loosens into beads and the ring stays full while it waits up to 1.5s for the cover; only then does it fall back to returning the grains home
Buttons renamed to Pour into next and Collapse into next; Shift with R or Shift with a hold rebuilds the current cover, and the tray aria-label says so

Clump flights use a long asymmetric ease-in-out (slow lift, longer settle) in place of the overshooting ease-out-back, so nothing snaps or overshoots
Flights are slower and steadier: clumps glide for about 1.4 to 2.3s and the swap lands within about 2.9s (was 1.7s); in an offline simulation of both versions the median peak grain speed falls from about 1,100 to 150 cells a second and the largest single-frame jump from 55 cells to under 6
The next picture resolves in one graceful order: grains come to rest from the bottom of the cover upward on a soft, noise-warped front centred under where you pressed
Each grain rides its clump and only settles out of it over the last third of the clump's glide, so clumps no longer burst open as they land
Clumps are split by source patch and by which part of the next cover they are bound for, so each clump drifts to one area instead of converging on the middle and bursting outward
Each clump arrives with its earliest grain and leaves just early enough to get there, so departures follow the same bottom-up order
Arcs are small and soft (6% of the distance, eased), the curl drift is a quarter of its old strength and moves more slowly, like sand in water
Grains swell only 10% mid-flight instead of 30%, and the shrink-then-pop on landing is gone
Gathering into clumps and the curl drift both ease in and out (sine squared), so there is no jolt at take-off
Grains are drawn in landing order so moving sand always passes over settled sand instead of flickering behind it
The picture softens into beads over 420ms with an ease-in-out (was 180ms), and the settled beads melt into the finished cover over 900ms with an ease-in-out (was a 340ms snap)
The tray no longer squashes on landing, and the hold ring fades out softly instead of popping
Collapse into next releases its rows over 1s with gentler gravity and then rises into the next cover with the same calm settle
Shift-hold rebuild uses the same calm settle on slightly shorter flights
If the next cover is not ready in time, or staging changes mid-hold, the beads now fade back into the picture instead of snapping
Load: the tray fades in with a soft focus-pull and no scale, the colour placeholder fades out after the cover is visible, and the demonstration crumble waits until the fade has finished, moves more slowly, and is skipped if you have already started rubbing
Planning is spread over three frames (write, schedule, draw order) in a new sandFlight.js module
